source_kind: library derivation from pinned standard MGF and hyperbolic-cosine series; no external paper theorem-number claim
public_topic: Even moments of a subgaussian real random variable
statements: For every real x and natural m, x^(2m)/(2m)! <= cosh(x).

For any probability measure mu, real random variable X satisfying Mathlib HasSubgaussianMGF(X,c,mu), c a nonnegative real, and natural m, abs(X)^(2m) is integrable and its integral is at most (2m)! exp(1/2) c^m. Natural zero powers use the usual 0^0=1 convention; c=0 and m=0 are included.
proof_graph: The nonnegative even series of cosh bounds each individual even-power term.
Subgaussian exponential integrability implies all finite absolute moments are integrable.
Integrate the cosh coefficient inequality and use both signed MGF bounds exp(c*t^2/2).
For c>0 set t=1/sqrt(c); for c=0 use the standard almost-sure-zero consequence, handling m=0 separately.
dependency_search: Current pinned public probability modules and Mathlib SubGaussian file expose mgf bounds, all-p MemLp and tail bounds, but no named quantitative even-moment producer was found. Reuse those actual parents.
intended_placement: Probability / concentration textbook supplement; generic public library theorem
scope_boundary: This produces moments only from a proved subgaussian MGF. It does not produce a diffusion, an LSI, an evolving-law curvature estimate, or whole-model coverage.
